claim: Chromatin remodelers are members of the extensive superfamily 2 (SF2) group of ATPase motors found in all kingdoms of life.
source: Chromatin remodelers are members of the extensive superfamily 2 (SF2) group of ATPase motors found in all kingdoms of life (Flaus and Owen-Hughes, 2001; Flaus et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Flaus and Owen-Hughes, 2001 and Flaus et al., 2006

claim: SF2 ATPases possess a bi-lobed architecture, with a central ATP-binding pocket defined by two RecA-like domains.
source: SF2 ATPases possess a bi-lobed architecture, with a central ATP-binding pocket defined by two RecA-like domains (reviewed in Singleton et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Singleton et al., 2007 review

claim: Conformational changes driven by cycles of ATP binding and hydrolysis enable many SF2 enzymes to translocate in an inchworm fashion along nucleic acids.
source: Like the architecturally similar SF1 ATPases, both lobes of the motor coordinate in binding to DNA or RNA, with conformational changes driven by cycles of ATP binding and hydrolysis enabling many SF2 enzymes to translocate in an inchworm fashion along nucleic acids (Singleton et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citation to Singleton et al., 2007

claim: Canonical nucleosomes consist of two copies each of the four core histones (H2A, H2B, H3, and H4) wrapped by ~146 base pairs (bp) of duplex DNA.
source: Canonical nucleosomes consist of two copies each of the four core histones (H2A, H2B, H3, and H4) wrapped by ~146 base pairs (bp) of duplex DNA (reviewed in McGinty and Tan, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citation to McGinty and Tan, 2015 review

claim: Several chromatin remodelers have been shown to ratchet DNA past the histone core in single bp steps, known as nucleosome sliding.
source: Several chromatin remodelers have been shown to ratchet DNA past the histone core in single bp steps, known as nucleosome sliding, which is consistent with the basic inchworm mechanism of DNA translocation (Deindl et al., 2013; Harada et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Deindl et al., 2013 and Harada et al., 2016

claim: DNA could be shifted past the histone core by twist diffusion, where transfer of one or a small number of bps from one DNA segment to the next results in DNA displacement.
source: One of the earliest models for nucleosome motion suggested that DNA could be shifted past the histone core by twist diffusion, where transfer of one or a small number of bps from one DNA segment to the next results in DNA displacement (van Holde and Yager, 2003; van Holde and Yager, 1985).
evidence: Supported by citations to van Holde and Yager, 2003 and van Holde and Yager, 1985

claim: Each segment of nucleosomal DNA that gains or loses a bp relative to the canonical nucleosome experiences a change in both DNA length and twist and is referred to as a twist defect.
source: Each segment of nucleosomal DNA that gains or loses a bp relative to the canonical nucleosome experiences a change in both DNA length and twist and is referred to as a twist defect.
evidence: This is a definition provided in the manuscript

claim: Diffusion of twist defects could explain nucleosome movement by chromatin remodelers.
source: In addition to explaining heat-induced movement of the histone core along DNA, it was proposed that diffusion of twist defects could explain nucleosome movement by chromatin remodelers (van Holde and Yager, 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to van Holde and Yager, 2003

claim: Chromatin remodelers shift DNA off the nucleosome in single bp steps.
source: Indeed, experimental support for twist diffusion comes from the observations that chromatin remodelers shift DNA off the nucleosome in single bp steps (Deindl et al., 2013; Harada et al., 2016) and can induce and are sensitive to torsional strain (Gavin et al., 2001; Havas et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to Deindl et al., 2013 and Harada et al., 2016

claim: Chromatin remodelers can induce and are sensitive to torsional strain.
source: Indeed, experimental support for twist diffusion comes from the observations that chromatin remodelers shift DNA off the nucleosome in single bp steps (Deindl et al., 2013; Harada et al., 2016) and can induce and are sensitive to torsional strain (Gavin et al., 2001; Havas et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citations to Gavin et al., 2001 and Havas et al., 2000

claim: INO80 appears to translocate on DNA near the edge of the nucleosome around superhelix location 6 (SHL6).
source: In contrast to INO80, which appears to translocate on DNA near the edge of the nucleosome around superhelix location 6 (SHL6) (Ayala et al., 2018; Brahma et al., 2017; Eustermann et al., 2018), Chd1, ISWI, and SWI/SNF-type remodelers translocate on nucleosomal DNA at the internal SHL2 site, located ~20 bp from the nucleosome dyad (Deindl et al., 2013; McKnight et al., 2011; Saha et al., 2005; Schwanbeck et al., 2004; Zofall et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ayala et al., 2018; Brahma et al., 2017; Eustermann et al., 2018

claim: Chd1, ISWI, and SWI/SNF-type remodelers translocate on nucleosomal DNA at the internal SHL2 site, located ~20 bp from the nucleosome dyad.
source: In contrast to INO80, which appears to translocate on DNA near the edge of the nucleosome around superhelix location 6 (SHL6) (Ayala et al., 2018; Brahma et al., 2017; Eustermann et al., 2018), Chd1, ISWI, and SWI/SNF-type remodelers translocate on nucleosomal DNA at the internal SHL2 site, located ~20 bp from the nucleosome dyad (Deindl et al., 2013; McKnight et al., 2011; Saha et al., 2005; Schwanbeck et al., 2004; Zofall et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Deindl et al., 2013; McKnight et al., 2011; Saha et al., 2005; Schwanbeck et al., 2004; Zofall et al., 2006

claim: Recent work has revealed the organization of Chd1 domains on the nucleosome in the ADP·BeF3– state, which has defined the positioning and orientation of ATPase motor domains on nucleosomal DNA at SHL2.
source: Recent work has revealed the organization of Chd1 domains on the nucleosome in the ADP·BeF3– state, which has defined the positioning and orientation of ATPase motor domains on nucleosomal DNA at SHL2 (Farnung et al., 2017; Nodelman et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Farnung et al., 2017; Nodelman et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018

claim: Cross-linking requires van der Waals contact between the reactive nitrene moiety of APB and its DNA target, which corresponds to a reach of ~11 Å from the Cα of the APB-modified cysteine.
source: Cross-linking requires van der Waals contact between the reactive nitrene moiety of APB and its DNA target, which corresponds to a reach of ~11 Å from the Cα of the APB-modified cysteine (Pendergrast et al., 1992).
evidence: Supported by citation to Pendergrast et al., 1992

claim: The Chd1 domain placement based on cross-linking modeling yielded a structurally similar placement as cryoEM complexes solved in an ADP·BeF3– state.
source: Our modeling, which was based on nine different cross-linking sites, yielded a structurally similar placement of Chd1 domains as cryoEM complexes solved in an ADP·BeF3– state (Farnung et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: Comparison between the authors' modeling and published cryoEM structures

claim: ADP·BeF3– has been cited as a ground-state mimic of ATP.
source: While ADP·BeF3– has been cited as a ground-state mimic of ATP, the BeF3– moiety as the gamma phosphate mimic can occupy a range of positions relative to ADP, depending on the system and conditions, and thus can also resemble a hydrolysis intermediate (Kagawa et al., 2004; Thomsen and Berger, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kagawa et al., 2004 and Thomsen and Berger, 2009

claim: The BeF3– moiety as the gamma phosphate mimic can occupy a range of positions relative to ADP, depending on the system and conditions, and thus can also resemble a hydrolysis intermediate.
source: While ADP·BeF3– has been cited as a ground-state mimic of ATP, the BeF3– moiety as the gamma phosphate mimic can occupy a range of positions relative to ADP, depending on the system and conditions, and thus can also resemble a hydrolysis intermediate (Kagawa et al., 2004; Thomsen and Berger, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to Kagawa et al., 2004 and Thomsen and Berger, 2009

claim: Chd1 interacts with both strands of the minor groove at SHL2.
source: Chd1 interacts with both strands of the minor groove at SHL2 (Farnung et al., 2017; Nodelman et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to Farnung et al., 2017 and Nodelman et al., 2017

claim: Chd1 is positioned to translocate along the tracking strand in a 3' to 5' direction.
source: Like the SWI/SNF-type remodeler RSC, Chd1 is positioned to translocate along the tracking strand in a 3' to 5' direction (Farnung et al., 2017; Nodelman et al., 2017; Saha et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citations to Farnung et al., 2017; Nodelman et al., 2017; Saha et al., 2005

claim: Cross-links for both ATPase lobes indicate a relatively fixed position of the motor at SHL2 in apo, ADP, and ATP-mimic states.
source: Consistent with this notion, cross-links for both ATPase lobes indicate a relatively fixed position of the motor at SHL2 in apo, ADP, and ATP-mimic states (Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental cross-linking data shown in Figure 1 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: Lobe 2 of the Chd1 remodeler changed contacts with DNA in a nucleotide-dependent fashion and was highly sensitive to DNA sequence.
source: As monitored by site-specific cross-linking, lobe 2 of the Chd1 remodeler changed contacts with DNA in a nucleotide-dependent fashion and was highly sensitive to DNA sequence (Figure 1).
evidence: Supported by experimental cross-linking data shown in Figure 1

claim: The open state of the Chd1 ATPase showed the capability of pulling DNA toward itself.
source: Remarkably, the open state of the Chd1 ATPase showed the capability of pulling DNA toward itself.
evidence: Based on experimental observations described in the manuscript

claim: On the TA-poor side of the Widom 601 nucleosome, Chd1 shifted a large segment of DNA across the histone surface by 1–3 nt.
source: On the TA-poor side of the Widom 601 nucleosome, Chd1 shifted a large segment of DNA across the histone surface by 1–3 nt.
evidence: Based on experimental cross-linking data

claim: The DNA shift toward the remodeler occurred in apo and ADP-bound states and was independent of nucleotide hydrolysis.
source: This DNA shift toward the remodeler occurred in apo and ADP-bound states and was independent of nucleotide hydrolysis (Figures 2 and 3).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2 and 3

claim: The cryoEM structure of the SWI/SNF ATPase bound to the nucleosome revealed significant distortions in DNA at the binding site, with 3–6 Å displacements of the sugar-phosphate backbone from its canonical path and some disruptions in base stacking interactions.
source: Recently, the cryoEM structure of the SWI/SNF ATPase bound to the nucleosome provided a first view of how an open ATPase motor engages with the nucleosome (Liu et al., 2017). This structure, which preferentially bound the TA-poor SHL+2 site of the Widom 601 nucleosome, revealed significant distortions in DNA at the binding site, with 3–6 Å displacements of the sugar-phosphate backbone from its canonical path and some disruptions in base stacking interactions.
evidence: Supported by citation to Liu et al., 2017

claim: The nucleotide-free states of SF1 (RecBCD) and SF2 (NS3) ATPases were previously found to unwind DNA duplexes, independently of nucleotide-driven translocation.
source: The nucleotide-free states of SF1 (RecBCD) and SF2 (NS3) ATPases were previously found to unwind DNA duplexes, independently of nucleotide-driven translocation (Farah and Smith, 1997; Levin et al., 2005; Singleton et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citations to Farah and Smith, 1997; Levin et al., 2005; Singleton et al., 2004

claim: For NS3, it was proposed that a nucleotide-free unwinding step is achieved by favorable protein-DNA interactions, with the motor acting as a Brownian ratchet to capture DNA in a transiently melted state.
source: For NS3, it was proposed that a nucleotide-free unwinding step is achieved by favorable protein-DNA interactions, with the motor acting as a Brownian ratchet to capture DNA in a transiently melted state (Levin et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Levin et al., 2005

claim: With ADP·BeF3– and transition state analogs, Chd1 appeared to reinforce the canonical structure of nucleosomal DNA at SHL2, without a bulge.
source: Compared to the open apo and ADP-bound states of the motor, nucleotide-bound states of Chd1 containing ATP mimics and transition state analogs favored distinct organizations of nucleosomal DNA at SHL2. With ADP·BeF3– and transition state analogs, Chd1 appeared to reinforce the canonical structure of nucleosomal DNA at SHL2, without a bulge.
evidence: Based on experimental observations described in the manuscript

claim: Chd1 binding at SHL–2 shifted DNA over the dyad by ~1 bp with transition state analogs, indicating an incompatibility with the SHL–2 bulge favored by apo and ADP-bound states.
source: As shown with the 601[insert(+1) TA-rich] nucleosome variant, Chd1 binding at SHL–2 shifted DNA over the dyad by ~1 bp with transition state analogs, indicating an incompatibility with the SHL–2 bulge favored by apo and ADP-bound states (Figure 6).
evidence: Supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6

claim: Chd1-nucleosome complexes bound to ADP·BeF3– and visualized by cryoEM show only modest perturbations of nucleosomal DNA at the bound SHL2 sites.
source: These observations agree with Chd1-nucleosome complexes bound to ADP·BeF3– and visualized by cryoEM, which show only modest perturbations of nucleosomal DNA at the bound SHL2 sites (Farnung et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Farnung et al., 2017 and Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018

claim: Chd1 binds at SHL2 and translocates DNA toward the nucleosome dyad.
source: Like ISWI- and SWI/SNF-type remodelers, Chd1 binds at SHL2 and translocates DNA toward the nucleosome dyad (Farnung et al., 2017; McKnight et al., 2011; Nodelman et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Farnung et al., 2017; McKnight et al., 2011; Nodelman et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2018

claim: The core mechanism for translocating nucleosomal DNA past the histone core arises from the ATPase motor enforcing unique geometries of DNA at its binding site.
source: We propose that the core mechanism for translocating nucleosomal DNA past the histone core arises from the ATPase motor enforcing unique geometries of DNA at its binding site (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the authors' experimental findings

claim: DNA translocation is initiated by the open form of the remodeler ATPase motor binding at SHL2, which draws ~1 bp into a bulge and results in DNA on the entry gyre of the nucleosome being shifted toward the remodeler by ~1 bp.
source: According to this model, DNA translocation is initiated by the open form of the remodeler ATPase motor binding at SHL2, which draws ~1 bp into a bulge and results in DNA on the entry gyre of the nucleosome being shifted toward the remodeler by ~1 bp.
evidence: This is part of the proposed model based on experimental findings

claim: Subsequent closure of the ATPase cleft upon ATP binding and hydrolysis forces a redistribution of the bulged DNA, with collapse of the bulge pushing ~1 bp onto the DNA segment toward the dyad, on the other side of the motor.
source: Subsequent closure of the ATPase cleft upon ATP binding and hydrolysis forces a redistribution of the bulged DNA, with collapse of the bulge pushing ~1 bp onto the DNA segment toward the dyad, on the other side of the motor.

claim: Nucleosomes are expected to respond to DNA translocation by twist diffusion.
source: Nucleosomes are expected to respond to DNA translocation by twist diffusion.

claim: Twist diffusion defines the core mechanism by which remodelers shift nucleosomal DNA.
source: Our data reveal that twist diffusion also defines the core mechanism by which remodelers shift nucleosomal DNA.

claim: The pre- and post-shifted states correspond to distinct twist states of nucleosomal DNA.
source: Our data indicate that the pre- and post-shifted states correspond to distinct twist states of nucleosomal DNA.

claim: The DNA bulge caused by the apo/ADP states of the ATPase motor results in DNA undertwisting at the binding site.
source: By accommodating ~1 additional bp, the DNA bulge caused by the apo/ADP states of the ATPase motor results in DNA undertwisting at the binding site (using the definition that more bp/turn means less twist per bp).

claim: Returning DNA conformation to a more canonical form, favored by restructuring of the motor as it hydrolyzes ATP, forces the twist defect onto the neighboring DNA segment.
source: Returning DNA conformation to a more canonical form, favored by restructuring of the motor as it hydrolyzes ATP, forces the twist defect onto the neighboring DNA segment.

source: The first and many subsequent crystal structures of the nucleosome showed that ±1 bp differences in DNA length readily occur at SHL2 and SHL5 (Luger et al., 1997; reviewed in McGinty and Tan, 2015; and Muthurajan et al., 2003).

claim: Twist diffusion has recently been visualized in molecular simulations of nucleosomes, where DNA segments bounded by minor groove contacts spontaneously gain or lose single bps in coordination with adjacent DNA.
source: Twist diffusion has recently been visualized in molecular simulations of nucleosomes, where DNA segments bounded by minor groove contacts spontaneously gain or lose single bps in coordination with adjacent DNA (Brandani et al., 2018).
